speaker: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross
quote: Drones are a defining threat for our time
points: JIATF-401 focuses on small, software-defined, hardware-enabled, low-cost, attritable solutions; Services keep Title 10 responsibility for larger systems.
Wants kinetic interceptors without explosive warheads for homeland use (low collateral damage).
Standardizing comms protocols for plug-and-play sensors/effectors; standard test measurement protocols to end 'demo fatigue'.
Marketplace will list hundreds of components; thinking interchangeable parts, not only full stacks.
Pursuing expansion of 10 U.S.C. 130i to all DoW installations and data sharing with DHS (6 U.S.C. 124n).
Groups 1 and 2 UAS under-resourced compared with Group 3.
um_relevance: Direct signal: JIATF-401 explicitly seeks non-explosive kinetic interceptors for homeland use — UM's tethered-rope v1 and kinetic-ram Block 2 sit in exactly this lane.

speaker: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross
quote: The threat posed from unmanned systems is going to far exceed the threat that we saw from IEDs.
points: JIATF-401 online marketplace is live (Ross called it 'clunky').
Common C2 architecture contract expected within months (became Anduril Lattice, March 2026).
Installations should be able to order equipment and set it up 'like a Ring doorbell' without vendor technicians.
'We didn't want to wait for a 9/11 event inside the United States.'
um_relevance: Ease-of-deployment is a stated buying criterion — UM's canister launch with no vehicle or crew setup lines up with the 'Ring doorbell' standard.

speaker: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross
venue: Industry Day, Hilton Alexandria Mark Center, VA
quote: What we need is a layered defense: awareness, different capabilities and an ecosystem that works together
points: Priorities: proliferation of low-cost sUAS; making c-sUAS products accessible to customers; expanding the industrial base; closing integration gaps across DoW and interagency.
um_relevance: Industry days are the primary on-ramp; UM should register for the next one and the marketplace.

speaker: Brig. Gen. Matthew Ross
quote: We need to get outside that perimeter to sense in depth
points: JIATF-401 reports to the Deputy Secretary of War; Ross also advises the CJCS on C-UAS.
Priorities: homeland defense, warfighter lethality, joint training.
Testing Bumblebee V1/V2 kinetic interceptors with automatic target recognition and software-updatable algorithms.
Aggregating demand across DoD and interagency so U.S. industry builds breadth and depth.
Layered defense on 1,954-mile southern border; $20M+ of C-UAS tech allocated there.
um_relevance: Sensing in depth beyond the perimeter favors airborne sensors — UM's onboard radar + EO/IR interceptor is a forward sensor as well as an effector.

speaker: Brent G. Ingraham
role: Assistant Secretary of the Army (Acquisition, Logistics & Technology)
quote: These vehicles span counter-UAS capabilities from sensors to effectors to C2 systems, giving us options as requirements emerge.
points: Multi-vendor marketplace enforces strict open-architecture standards; intent to avoid vendor lock-in.
Only ~$50M obligated at award; the rest depends on FY27 appropriations (CR to mid-Dec 2026).
um_relevance: Open-architecture compliance (Lattice/C2 integration) is now a gating requirement to be ordered from these vehicles.

speaker: Col. Tony Lindh
quote: Expects to sign additional IDIQs before the end of next month to reach the full $7B ceiling (paraphrase).
points: $4.15B awarded to 10 vendors on 2026-09-29 plus ~$1B earlier (AV, CACI); remaining ceiling to be awarded by end of October 2026.
um_relevance: Time-critical: the remaining ~$1.85B of IDIQ ceiling is being placed in October 2026. Even if UM is too early to win a base award, it should learn the evaluation criteria and target the next on-ramp.

speaker: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross
quote: identify an urgent warfighter need, test available solutions against a common standard, make a data-driven decision, and move immediately toward delivering the capability.
points: Grizzly (Lockheed Martin) selected after Aug 17-28, 2026 Yuma Proving Ground shoot-off vs Group 3 UAS with PAE Fires.
um_relevance: The JIATF-401 model is test-then-buy: getting into a characterization event is the path to an award.

speaker: Dan Driscoll
quote: within about eight days, we were able to purchase … 13,000 Merops
points: Merops ~$15k each, expected below $10k at scale, vs $30-50k per Shahed.
'That puts us on the right end of the cost curve, and we will make that trade all day long.'
um_relevance: Proves the Army will buy interceptor drones in the tens of thousands, fast, when cost per kill beats the threat. UM's $1,600 modelled cost per kill has to be proven against this benchmark.

speaker: Brig. Gen. Curtis King
role: Commanding General, 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command
quote: enables us to kill [enemies] very effectively and at a much lower cost
points: Merops described as 'very lethal'; NATO allies Poland and Romania also operate it.
um_relevance: Operational users in Europe value low cost per kill above all; UM must show cost per kill and reuse.

speaker: Karen S. Evans
quote: We knew we needed to act quickly to keep the World Cup safe from the rising threat of unmanned aircraft systems
points: $250M to 11 World Cup host states + National Capital Region; awarded 25 days after the application deadline.
Second $250M tranche to all states and territories in FY2027.
um_relevance: State and local agencies now hold C-UAS money and (after SAFER SKIES) limited mitigation authority — a second customer base for a capture effector legal in populated airspace.

speaker: Markwayne Mullin
quote: These awards mark an important step in strengthening DHS's ability to respond to unauthorized and malicious unmanned aircraft systems.
points: DHS $1.5B department-wide C-UAS IDIQ (S&T). Justin Napolitano (DHS CSO) and Pedro Allende (Under Secretary S&T) also quoted.
Allende called standard contracting timelines a hindrance and sought renewed Other Transaction Authority.
um_relevance: DHS buys through prime integrators (Leidos, CACI, BAE, Anduril, etc.); UM's DHS path is as a subcontracted effector under a Track-1 holder.

speaker: NORTHCOM spokesperson / Gen. Gregory Guillot
quote: There have been several incursions, but we have not determined nefarious intent.
points: NORTHCOM's Flyaway Kit jammed a sUAS over a 'strategic' installation in the first hours of Operation Epic Fury (began 2026-02-28).
Incursions reported at Fort McNair and Barksdale AFB; more Flyaway Kits due spring 2026.
um_relevance: Homeland base incursions are real and continuing; jamming is the default response, and it fails against RF-silent drones — UM's core wedge.
